whatShips: What is open in the account
featIpDesc: Give it a host you already operate. The run lists reachable ports, service versions, and known CVEs by severity. Outside-in only. No SSH into the box. No agent for this step.
featDomainDesc: One outside-in snapshot: DNS, TLS and expiry, security headers, detected stack. Useful when a forgotten subdomain or a dying cert would surprise you. Posture, not a test of booking logic.
featMobileDesc: Upload the APK, AAB, or IPA you give guests or staff. Risky permissions, exported components, and secrets sitting in the binary get flagged before that build hits a store.
featAttachDesc: Park the target on an interval. Every run diffs the last one. A new open port shows up as a change. A single scan you forget is not a control.
featWorkspaceDesc: NOC, sysadmin, and the property contact read one trail. No PDF ping-pong. Roles and invites per org. Credits stay on each login, not in a shared pot.
featAssetsDesc: Register IPs, domains, and apps under the names the team already uses, so a ticket says "front-desk PMS" instead of a bare address. Each plan has a hard cap. The list stays honest.
featGuardDesc: One wazuh-agent per VM. It reports what is installed and running, then raises critical alerts. Inventory plus alarm on the box. Thin on purpose: not a SIEM console, and not a dashboard you babysit.
featUptimeDesc: Hit a URL or TCP port from outside. Record when it stops answering. Reachability only. It does not read CVEs. It is not an SLA on your rack or your upstream.
featCreditsDesc: Each scan draws from the balance on your account. A busy audit month spends more than a quiet one. Nothing is metered in secret. This page does not list prices.
heroEyebrow: Attaches to colo, VPS, and hospitality already on the invoice
heroHeadline: See what the internet sees on boxes you already pay for.
heroProduct: Attaches to colo, VPS, and hospitality already on the invoice
heroSub: The rack, the VPS, and the property uplink are already on the invoice. Sinexis attaches to that bill: an outside-in snapshot of IPs, domains, and mobile builds, a schedule that diffs each run, then one thin agent on the VM for inventory and critical alerts. A schedule is not 24/7 SIEM. Host Protect reads disk through a helper on the machine and returns empty when the disk is clean. One wazuh-agent per host. Not a human pentest.
authSubtitle: Sinexis. Attaches to colo, VPS, and hospitality already on the invoice
notFoundBody: That URL is not a Sinexis page. Go home, or sign in to open your workspace, scans, and Guard hosts.
stepScanDesc: Pick one IP, domain, or mobile build you own. The engine runs from the internet side. You get an HTML report you can hand to a client or an auditor.
stepAttachDesc: Set the interval to how often the infra actually changes. Weekly, monthly, your call. Each run diffs the last, so you read the delta instead of the whole report again.
stepWorkspaceDesc: Invite the team into one org. Assets get names people already use. History lives in one place. Tonight's shift sees the last findings.
stepGuardDesc: Enroll one wazuh-agent on the VM. It reports installed packages and running services, then raises critical alerts. That is the loop: Scan → Attach → Workspace → Guard.
siemNote: SIEM log search and Cases (incident tickets in our Postgres, not a Wazuh plugin) sit behind an ops flag. They are not sold as a live feature on this page. Host WAF runs in your nginx on your server. Never on the Sinexis edge.
faqAuthQ: Do I need written permission to scan?
faqAuthA: Yes. Scan only hosts, domains, and apps you own or are authorized in writing to test. If you run a property or a client rack, get that paper before the first run. Unauthorized scanning is not allowed.
faqPentestQ: Is a person going to pentest us?
faqPentestA: No. This is automated outside-in scanning on a schedule. It finds exposed services, weak TLS, missing headers, and known CVEs. It does not walk business logic, chained abuse, or your booking flow. If a contract still needs a manual pentest, keep that engagement. Use this between those dates.
faqDataA: Findings and reports stay in your workspace, visible to members you invite. Retention is in the privacy policy. Do not upload credentials or secrets you are not allowed to store off your own systems.
faqGuardQ: How is Guard different from SIEM and Host Protect?
faqGuardA: Guard is the thin agent view: machine inventory plus critical alerts, no log-hunting UI. SIEM is log search plus Cases, which are incident tickets in our Postgres, off by default, not sold live here. Host Protect is a helper on the VM that reads web directories for on-box malware. If the helper is missing or a path is unreachable, we say so and return no hits. We do not invent malware to fill a screen.
faqAgentQ: Two agents on the same VM?
faqAgentA: No. One wazuh-agent per machine, enrolled once to your org. Host Protect is a helper script on that same machine, not a second daemon competing for the box.
